name: TC Electronic FireworX
source: TC Electronic 'FireworX MIDI specification' V1.00 1999/07/20 (Word doc 'FireworX MIDI spec.doc', 5 pp.; Audiofanzine media 471618 = tcelectronic.com/media/FireworX_MIDI_spec.pdf = cdn-downloads.tcelectronic.com/media/216691/tc_electronic_fireworx_midi_sysex_specifications.pdf, byte-identical, via web.archive.org). FireworX User's Manual (English, v1.0 text, MIDI chart dated January 1998; ManualsLib PDF with the 400-preset factory list appended) for the parameter model, routing and I/O Setup. TC factory preset list (tc_electronic_fireworx_presets.pdf). Cross-checks: TC M-One MIDI spec V2.00 (same header/type family, model 0x44), NothNoth/M6000Protocol (SYXTYPE names, model IDs M-One 44 / D-Two 45 / M6000 46), SoundDiver users list 2000-12-10 (TC developer: a partial preset dump 'will update the preset as if the entire preset has been recalled ... one second of muted silence'). No open-source FireworX editor exists (KnobKraft, Ctrlr, Edisyn, SoundDiver: none); tekfunk/fireworx-live (Max for Live) uses only program change + CCs.

deviceId.rule: Byte 4 = the unit's 'Sysex device ID' (I/O Setup > MIDI). The manuals give no range; TC's siblings of this generation use 0-126 (G-System manual) with 127 unconfirmed as 'all'. Keep the editor and the unit on the same number (default 0). Replies carry the unit's own ID in byte 4.
deviceId.sweep: If a request gets no reply, the driver may sweep dev 0-126 with the same read-only request (one at a time, 300 ms each) and keep the first that answers (prefs 'dev'), like the Yamaha driver does.

tc.numbers14: Every 2-byte number (preset, count, address, size, packet count) is 14-bit, 7 bits per byte, MSB first: [n >> 7 & 7F, n & 7F].
tc.nibbles: Binary data travels as nibble pairs, high nibble first: byte b -> [b >> 4, b & 0F]. A dump of N data bytes is 2N nibble bytes followed by ONE checksum byte.
tc.checksum: checksum = (-(sum of the DATA BYTES)) & 7F -- computed over the reassembled 8-bit bytes, not over the nibble bytes (TC spec, 'Binary data'). Receiver check: (sum(data) + checksum) & 7F == 0.
tc.modelNote: 0x40 = FireworX (TC 'FireworX MIDI specification' V1.00, 1999-07-20, applies to software 2.00+). Siblings: M-One 0x44, D-Two 0x45, M6000 0x46.

presetNumbers.note: Spec: 0x0000 edit buffer, 0x0001-0x0190 factory (400), 0x0801-0x08C8 user (200 positions), 0x1001-0x1320 card (800 positions). Preset number = bank*128 + index, i.e. user n (1-based) = 2048 + n -> bytes 10 nn; card n = 4096 + n -> bytes 20 nn (n > 127 carries into the MSB). Same numbering as program change with bank select in 'Into all banks' mapping (bank 16 = user, bank 32 = card).

messageTypes.note: Values from the spec's type table (40 10 11 44 45 46 48 50 20 21 24 28 hex). The spec's per-message listings disagree for five types -- Request Part is printed 45 (copy error), Request Packed 47, Delete 45 (copy error), Data Part 20, Data Packed 22. The table is internally systematic (data 20 + flag: 01 part, 04 packed, 08 empty), so it wins; the driver should ACCEPT both values on receive (21|20 for part replies, 24|22 for packed) and resolve the two genuine conflicts on first contact: send Request Packed as 48; if nothing comes back in 800 ms retry as 47 and remember which worked (prefs 'packedReq').

messages.name: Preset Recall
messages.reply: none (the unit loads that preset into the edit buffer)
messages.example: recall user 1 on dev 0: F0 00 20 1F 00 40 44 10 01 F7

messages.name: Preset Request
messages.reply: Preset Data (20) in EXPANDED format, or Preset Data Is Empty (28)

messages.name: Preset Request Part
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 46 pH pL aH aL sH sL F7
messages.reply: Preset Data Part (21) or Empty (28). a = start address in the expanded structure, s = byte count.
messages.example: 16 bytes from address 0 of the edit buffer: F0 00 20 1F 00 40 46 00 00 00 00 00 10 F7

messages.name: Preset Request Packed
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 48 pH pL cH cL F7
messages.reply: one Preset Data Packed (24) or Empty (28) per position; c = count of consecutive positions (0 or 1 = just that one; last = p + c - 1)

messages.name: Preset Delete
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 50 pH pL cH cL F7
messages.reply: none; unconditionally deletes the range (user or card bank per the start number). DESTRUCTIVE -- never sent by the editor except on an explicit user action.

messages.name: Preset Data
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 20 pH pL sH sL <2s nibbles> ck F7
messages.note: complete preset, EXPANDED format; s = data byte count. Sent by the unit in reply to 45; sent TO the unit with p = 0 it replaces the edit buffer.

messages.name: Preset Data Part
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 21 pH pL aH aL sH sL <2s nibbles> ck F7
messages.example: write 1 byte (05) at expanded address 0x123 of the edit buffer: F0 00 20 1F 00 40 21 00 00 02 23 00 01 00 05 7B F7

messages.name: Preset Data Packed
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 24 pH pL sH sL <2s nibbles> ck F7
messages.note: complete preset, PACKED (storage) format: variable size, only the routed effects; field addresses vary with the routing. Opaque to the editor -- store and resend unchanged.

messages.name: Preset Data Is Empty
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 28 pH pL cH cL F7
messages.note: reply only; c consecutive empty positions from p.

messages.name: User Bank Request
messages.reply: User Bank Header then Data Packets (entire user bank)

messages.name: User Bank Header
messages.note: n = number of data packets that follow (10 bytes total)

messages.name: User Bank Data Packet
messages.format: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 11 id <128 nibbles> ck F7
messages.note: 64 data bytes per packet (138 bytes total); id counts up from 0 (one byte -- wrap after 127 not documented). Also the format of front-panel 'User Bank to MIDI' and of pre-2.00 software.

formats.expanded: Edit-buffer representation: 'contains all elements available for construction of a preset ... all parameter adjustments are preserved regardless of routing' (spec). Fixed layout, so params have fixed byte addresses -- but TC never published the map. Size = the s field of the first Preset Data reply.
formats.packed: Storage representation for user/card presets: only routed effects, variable size and variable addresses. Recalling a preset sets all non-routed effects to defaults.
formats.addressMap: UNMAPPED. Every param's addr/size is null. See driverNotes (address discovery).

capabilities.paramWriteSysex: only once addresses are mapped (Preset Data Part)
capabilities.paramWriteCC: Alpha Mod, Ext 1-8, main vol, bypass, tempo, effect-key bypass
capabilities.storedRead: factory, user, card (expanded via 45, packed via 48)
capabilities.storedWrite: user, card: packed restore via 24 is the documented storage format; expanded 20 to a slot number is untested
capabilities.transmitsEdits: no parameter SysEx; transmits Alpha Mod wheel moves and effect-key bypass states on their assigned CCs

setup: Software 2.00 or later (shown at power-up). The TC SysEx spec only applies to 2.00+; 1.x units only do the front-panel user-bank bulk dump.
Cable both ways: interface out -> FireworX MIDI IN, FireworX MIDI OUT -> interface in (every read is a reply).
[I/O SETUP] > MIDI > Sysex device ID = 0 (the editor default; any value works if the editor is set to match).

[I/O SETUP] > MIDI > Basic Channel = the editor channel; Program change = Enabled. Bank Selection = Coarse and Mapping mode = Into all banks (2.00+) only matter for the program-change fallback -- the editor recalls presets by SysEx.

[I/O SETUP] > CTRL (setup bank 1): Alpha Mod. = MIDI basic / Controller 1; Ext. 1-8 = MIDI basic / Controllers 16-23; Main vol. = Controller 7; Bypass = Controller 24; Tempo = Controller 25; Effect bypass Dyn, Fil, For, Dis, Voc, Syn, Pit, Cho, Dly, Rev, Pan, EQ = Controllers 80-91. (Learn: cursor on the item, Enter, move the editor control.) These numbers are the editor defaults in params[].cc -- change both together if you prefer others.
[I/O SETUP] > MIDI > Alpha Mod. Local = On (the unit then transmits its wheel on Controller 1, which the editor mirrors). Set Off only if a MIDI loop echoes it back.

driverNotes: TC Electronic SysEx, FireworX (model 40h), software 2.00+. (1) FRAME: F0 00 20 1F dd 40 tt <data> F7; dd = Sysex device ID (default 0), tt = message type. Match replies on bytes 1-3 = 00 20 1F, byte 5 = 40, byte 6 = type; accept any dd if the user is unsure of the ID and adopt it (prefs 'dev'). (2) NUMBERS: preset/count/address/size are 14-bit, [n>>7, n&7F]. Preset numbers: 0 = edit buffer, 1-400 factory, 2049-2248 user, 4097-4896 card (= bank*128 + index; user n -> 10 nn, card n -> 20 nn). A bank entry's sysexBase + prog gives the number. (3) DATA: each 8-bit data byte -> two bytes (high nibble, low nibble), then one checksum byte = (-sum(data bytes)) & 7F over the reassembled bytes. Unpack: for i in 0..s-1: b[i] = (d[2i] << 4) | d[2i+1]; verify (sum(b) + ck) & 7F == 0. Example 41 7F -> 04 01 07 0F 40. (4) TYPES (spec's table; accept the listing variants on receive): 40 bank request, 10 bank header, 11 bank packet, 44 recall, 45 request, 46 request part, 48 request packed (47?), 50 delete (never automatic), 20 data (expanded), 21 data part (20?), 24 data packed (22?), 28 is-empty. (5) probe(): send Preset Request Packed for factory 1 (F0 00 20 1F dd 40 48 00 01 00 01 F7) and wait 800 ms for a 24/22 reply; on silence retry with type 47, then with Preset Request 45 for preset 1 (expanded, bigger). Whichever answers proves the link and fixes the packed-request opcode (prefs 'packedReq'). (6) requestPatch(): F0 00 20 1F dd 40 45 00 00 F7 -> Preset Data 20 (p = 0000). Parse: bytes 7-8 = preset, 9-10 = size s, then 2s nibbles, ck, F7. Keep the unpacked bytes as the mirror (like lastData in the nrpn driver) so unmodelled bytes survive; values = read each param with addr != null from the mirror. Until the address map exists values is {} and syx is the raw reply (still useful: backup, A/B by bytes, and it gives the expanded size). (7) sendPatch(values): write modelled params into a copy of the mirror, send Preset Data F0 00 20 1F dd 40 20 00 00 sH sL <nibbles> ck F7 (s = mirror length). The unit re-initialises the preset: expect ~1 s of muted audio (TC developer, 2000). Refuse if no mirror has been read yet (the size and all unmapped bytes would be unknown). (8) sendParam(p, v): if p.path == 'cc': midi.cc(channel, p.cc, v) -- live, no mute; this is the real-time path (Alpha Mod, Ext 1-8 via the preset's matrix links, main vol, bypass, tempo tap, effect-key bypass). Else if p.addr != null: Preset Data Part to the edit buffer, F0 00 20 1F dd 40 21 00 00 aH aL sH sL <nibbles> ck F7 with a = p.addr, s = p.size (update the mirror first; multi-byte order to be learned when mapping) -- also triggers the ~1 s re-init mute, so coalesce knob drags (send on release, or at most every ~1.2 s). Else (addr unmapped): do nothing and report 'not mapped yet'. (9) programChange(bi, prog): Preset Recall F0 00 20 1F dd 40 44 nH nL F7 with n = banks[bi].sysexBase + prog (needs a card for card banks). No reply; follow with requestPatch if the editor wants the new edit buffer (wait ~300 ms). Fallback without SysEx: CC0 (Coarse) = bank per 'Into all banks' + program change. (10) requestProgram(bi, prog): Preset Request 45 with n = sysexBase + prog -> expanded Preset Data 20 for that slot (the edit buffer is untouched) or Preset Data Is Empty 28 (return {values:{}, data:null, syx, name:''} for empty). Match the reply on type AND preset number bytes 7-8. For bulk name scans / backups use Request Packed 48 with a count (one 24 or 28 message per position; 28 may cover several positions via its count). (11) writeProgram(bi, prog, values): only banks with write:true. Documented path: resend a Preset Data Packed (24) captured from the unit, with its preset number bytes changed to the target (restores/moves presets). Editing path (untested): send expanded Preset Data 20 with p = target slot and the edited mirror. After either, wait >= 500 ms, read the slot back with 45 and compare (sameProgram). A Protect range on the unit silently refuses; no ACK exists. Never send Preset Delete (50) implicitly. (12) sameProgram(a, b): compare mirrors on mapped params only; until mapped, compare the whole expanded byte arrays excluding the preset-number field (the payload after the size bytes). (13) decode(ev): CC on the basic channel whose number equals a live param's cc -> [{param, value}] (Alpha Mod wheel moves, effect-key bypass states the unit sends at preset change / key press). SysEx: the unit does not transmit parameter edits. Ignore our own replies (inFlight counter as in the Roland driver). (14) BACKUP/RESTORE: user bank = Request Packed p=2049 c=200 (collect 24/28 until 200 positions are accounted for; allow ~60 s); restore = send each 24 unchanged. Legacy: User Bank Request 40 -> header 10 (packet count) + packets 11 (64 bytes each) -- keep raw. Pace restores >= 150 ms per message (a front-panel bank dump of a few hundred 138-byte packets takes up to a minute, i.e. the unit paces itself ~150 ms). (15) PACING: gapMs 20 between small messages; >= 150 ms between dump messages sent to the unit; >= 1000 ms after a Preset Data / Data Part / Recall before expecting stable audio or sending the next preset. Timeouts: 800 ms for small replies, 3 s for an expanded preset, 60 s for a 200-slot packed range. (16) ADDRESS DISCOVERY (makes the knobs real): requestPatch -> A; change ONE parameter on the front panel by one step -> requestPatch -> B; diff A/B = that param's addr (and width if two bytes move; note byte order and signedness from +/- steps). Repeat per param (per algorithm: select it, then walk its slots). Name: the preset name is printable ASCII -- find the 21+ byte run that matches the Recall display. Record the map as addr/size (+ encoding) on each param; algorithms' slots may share addresses per block instance (generic P1..Pn) or be separate per algorithm -- the diffs will tell, and the layout keys ({i}P1..) work either way if the driver resolves addr by (instance, algo, slot). The routing grid may be stored per cell or as per-block (column,row) -- move one block and diff.
uncertain: Expanded preset structure: TC published the messages but NOT the byte layout, size, name offset or value encoding of the expanded (edit buffer) format. Every param's addr/size is null; SysEx param editing and value decoding need the address-discovery procedure in driverNotes (16). TC support told a Max user (cycling74 forum) the MIDI spec is all that exists.

Five message types differ between the spec's type table and its message listings: Request Part 46 vs 45, Request Packed 48 vs 47, Delete 50 vs 45, Data Part 21 vs 20, Data Packed 24 vs 22. The table is used (the 45s are obvious copy errors; 20/21 and 22/24 are ambiguous). Driver: accept both on receive, probe 48 then 47 for the request.

Whether a Preset Data (20, expanded) sent with a USER/CARD preset number stores the preset into that slot is not stated; only the packed format is described as the storage format. writeProgram's editing path is therefore untested; the packed-restore path is the documented one.

Parameter changes by SysEx (Preset Data Part to the edit buffer) re-initialise the whole preset with ~1 s of muted audio (TC developer quoted on the SoundDiver list, Dec 2000, for the 2.x spec). Not a real-time path; the real-time path is CC to Alpha Mod / Ext 1-8 via the preset's matrix links.
Sysex device ID range is not printed (siblings: 0-126). Whether 127 = 'all' is unknown.
User Bank Data Packet id is one byte 'counting up from 0'; with more than 128 packets it presumably wraps (7-bit). Unverified.
Whether the unit accepts a User Bank Header/Packet stream without first arming Utility > MIDI to User Bank is not stated (the manual only describes the armed front-panel procedure).
Preset name length: not stated; the factory list contains a 21-character name ('Aggressive>>Impulse<<'), so 21 name params are modelled.

The editor-side CC numbers (Alpha 1, Ext 16-23, main vol 7, bypass 24, tempo 25, effect bypass 80-91) are this schema's recommendation, set on the unit in I/O Setup > CTRL; the unit has no fixed CC map. Bypass/effect-key polarity (which value = bypassed) is not documented -- the unit's own transmissions at preset change reveal it.
The manual's MIDI chart gives CC 0-119 while the CTRL page text says 0-127 / 1-127; keep assignments inside 1-119.
Routing: modelled as 64 grid cells (the Routing display's model). The stored form may be per-block (column,row) positions; how parallel branches join is drawn by the unit and not modelled.

Algorithm index order = the order the manual prints (routing list vs block pages differ in naming: Single/Dual Voice vs Fixed 1/2 Voice, Fixed/Modifiable EQ vs Fixed/Mod. Parametric). On-unit order and encoding unverified.

Most parameter ranges are not printed in the manual (only ~156 of 348 entries have a range or option list); unknown ranges are raw 0-127 placeholders flagged rangeKnown:false, with the manual's display range (if any) in displayRange or the algorithms table.
The v1.0-text manual is the only English manual found; 2.00 added 200 factory presets and the extended SysEx but no documented parameter changes. The French 'Rev 2 SW 2.00' manual has the same text.
